name: charge_target_update
comment: Sets the charger's constant-voltage target. Reached by a conditional branch from 0xB141 (jb acc.1 on XDATA 0x0490 bit 1) and not by any call, so the direct-call census in bank-call-targets.csv cannot seed it; this row is what puts it in the project.

name: charge_stress_update
comment: Age-derating section: the seconds/minutes counters at XDATA 0x09C7/0x09C8 and the stress accumulator at 0x09C9, tiered by pack temperature. The worked acceptance target for this pipeline per ec/ghidra/README.md.

name: check_0xB112
comment: First early-return gate of charge_target_update. What it tests was NOT decoded; the name is the one charge-target-derating.md uses for it and nothing more is claimed.

name: batt_temp_dK
comment: Returns pack temperature in decikelvin from XDATA 0x04A2/0x04A3; the 3030/3130 dK thresholds below are 29.9 C and 39.9 C.

name: cfg_cell_count_selector
comment: Yields 0xC0 or 0x80, which charge_target_update turns into a 4S/3S cell count. What configures it is not known.

name: stress_headroom
comment: Computes 65000 minus the stress counter minus 1, so the caller can skip the increment on borrow.

name: store_be16_a
comment: Cited by charge-target-derating.md as one of the two helpers that store 16-bit values big-endian (hi byte first). The two are not told apart by that file, hence the _a/_b pair rather than two confident names.

name: store_be16_b
comment: The second of the two big-endian 16-bit store helpers; see the note on 0xBB90.

name: tier_250_eligible
comment: One of the comparisons behind the 250 mV-per-cell derating tier (stress > 18144).

name: tier_200_eligible
comment: One of the comparisons behind the 200 mV-per-cell derating tier (stress > 14808).

name: mul16
comment: 16-bit multiply, called by charge_target_update to get cells x 4100 and again for the final target arithmetic.

name: be16_add
comment: Big-endian 16-bit add, used to accumulate the temperature-weighted stress increment.

name: limit_65000_minus_x
comment: Called from 0xBCF5 to compute 65000 - stress - 1.

name: manual_ctrl_profile_gate
comment: Sets CHARGING_PROFILE in FAN_CTRL then, if AP_OEM ENABLE_MANUAL_CTRL is clear, masks OEM_4 bits 4-5 to force the profile back to High Capacity. The tick that runs it is not identified; the file notes uniwill-laptop clears that bit at shutdown so the reset fires on every module unload by design

name: fan_table_mailbox_handler
comment: Handler for the 0x0F5D-0x0F5F mailbox: requires 0x0F5D=0xFD and 0x0F5E=0xC9, reads table selector 0x0F5F (1 Turbo, 2 Gaming, 3 Office, the last chosen between two Office tables by 0x0782 bit 2) and copies 0x30 bytes from each of a CODE pointer pair to 0x0F00 and 0x0F30. The trigger found is explicit host request, and whether some other path also calls the copy is not something a site scan can rule out

name: fan_mode_get
comment: Mode getter: masks 0x0751 with 0x90 to return only the USER and TURBO bits that distinguish the three fan modes, an independent confirmation of the vendor's mode encoding. It says nothing about whether the EC acts on a value the host wrote

name: seed_fan_table_base
comment: Seeds the fan-table CODE base as 0x60F2, a table of big-endian CODE pointer pairs from which the 0x888D handler copies; it is the routine called at 0xA828 inside the 0xA7C8 routine. The rest of this routine is not analysed in the file that establishes it

name: fan_table_base_offset_helper
comment: Helper called by the 0x888D handler when the 0x0F5F table selector is 2, annotated in the listing as yielding base + 0x00. Its own body is not decoded there, so the role is read off the call site only

name: add_full_product_to_dptr
comment: Keil index helper: multiplies A by B then adds the low byte of the product to DPL and the carry into DPH i.e. DPTR += A * B. The 0x07D0 sites reach it with B loaded from a record stride and DPTR loaded from an array base | The DPTR += A x B arithmetic helper in the same 0x10xx compiler-library neighbourhood as 0x10E8, 0x10C8 and 0x1041, but explicitly not one of them: it only adds to DPTR where those dereference it. The decode behind 0x04A6's handoffs belongs to pd-xdata-overlap.md; this file only cites the role | Adds the full A x B product to the incoming DPTR (MOV A,B retains the multiplication high byte for the ADDC into DPH), preserves R0-R7 and does no memory access, so the x2 its callers add is not truncated like the outer x0x38 term (cited from 3 files)

name: index_stride_77_addr_r1
comment: Stride 0x77 index helper returning the address halves in A:R1 - correction #74 supersedes the earlier R2:R1 reading - and the only one of the four multiply forms that keeps the full product: 0x089B + A * 0x77. No page term was resolved by this bounded decode

name: index_stride_77_r7
comment: Stride 0x77 helper reached from site 0xDA9B via 0xDAA3: it gives 0x0870 + low8(R7 * 0x77) so the high byte of the product is dropped while the low base addition still carries into the high byte

name: store_r7_at_dptr
comment: One of only two of the 25 handoff helpers that begins by storing rather than reading: 6 of the 0x07D0 sites hand DPTR to it so those sites are writes and not reads. The file does not trace the callers past the store

name: read_byte_to_r3_stride_60
comment: Handoff helper reached by 12 of the 0x07D0 sites: its first three instructions read the byte at DPTR copy it into R3 and load B with 0x60 so on the file's index reading it prepares a stride-0x60 index. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: read_byte_to_r3_stride_60_alt
comment: Handoff helper reached by 8 of the 0x07D0 sites and identical in its first three instructions to 0x357E: it reads the byte at DPTR copies it into R3 and loads B with 0x60. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: read_byte_to_r7_base_0420
comment: Handoff helper reached by 6 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR then points DPTR at 0x0420 and keeps the byte in R7. Only those three instructions are decoded here and 0x0420 is not otherwise identified

name: read_byte_to_r7_base_0408
comment: Handoff helper reached by 5 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR keeps it in R7 and points DPTR at 0x0408 which is the base the file names for the 0x60-byte records. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: read_byte_to_r7_set_r3_1
comment: Handoff helper reached by 4 of the 0x07D0 sites: it reads the byte at DPTR into R7 and loads R3 with 0x01. Only those three instructions are decoded here

name: store_first_handoff_helper
comment: The other of the two handoff helpers that begins by storing: the file groups it with the 18 entry points carrying 1-3 sites each and records that all of those but this one begin movx a,@dptr. Its body is not decoded here and its exact site count is not stated

name: index_stride_5e_from_07d6
comment: Head of the routine whose tail at 0x34D9 is the stride-0x5E handoff entry: the head loads 0x07D6 where 0x34D9's callers load 0x07D0 and the two share the same multiply. This tail-sharing is the file's reason the entry addresses look unaligned

name: call_returns_with_dptr_loaded
comment: Called immediately before seven of the eight 0x07D0 sites that decode with no movx in the window - those sites are lcall 0xF739 ; mov dptr,#0x07d0 ; ret - so this file describes it only as returning with DPTR left pointing at the byte. Its body is not decoded here

name: store_3byte_r3r2r1
comment: Stores R3 then R2 then R1 at DPTR with an inc dptr between each, rets at 0x10F0. Three of the eleven handoff sites reach it this way (0x5F03, 0x81A8, 0xB7A4), each writing three bytes of the 0x07Ex block

name: write4xdata_from_r4_r7
comment: 4-byte store from R4:R5:R6:R7, rets at 0x104C. One handoff site (0x6610) uses it, which is how a 0x07E5 site reaches up to 0x07E8. Not one of the lcall 0x104D inline-argument routines that #36 owns | Four-byte XDATA writer relative to the entry pointer P: writes P..P+3 from R4..R7 and returns DPTR=P+3, preserving R4-R7. The stores are the MOVX instructions at 0x1042/45/48/4B, and this establishes a four-byte copy on one path, not a record width (cited from 2 files)

name: store_2byte_r6r7_then_0x10c8
comment: 2-byte store from R6:R7, then reloads DPTR with 0x07D8 and calls 0x10C8 on it, before ljmp 0x0F45. Reached by lcall from the 0x6482 and 0x64AD sites, and what it then does with the 0x07D8 pointer is not read in this file

name: c_startup_idata_clear
comment: The ITE8850-PD image's own reset vector lands here and the head is the textbook Keil/SDCC IDATA clear: R0 counting 0x7F down to 0x00 with @r0 zeroed, then DPTR set to 0x0000. It is the evidence that 0x20000 is a second program, and it is PD-image code, not EC code

name: load_1byte_to_r6
comment: 1-byte load, returned in R6, leaving 0x67 in B. Reached by lcall from the 0x8F94 site. The 0x67 is recorded as the instruction's literal, not as a decoded unit

name: load_xdata_to_r0_r1_r2_or_r3
comment: The routine 0x383A hands DPTR to; the head listed here is a 3-byte load into R0:R1:R2. The file records the 3-byte read as the same reading as its 0x10C8 table row, not as a traced caller | Four MOVX reads into R0-R3 with three INC DPTR, ending in an ordinary RET; it preserves R7 and does not touch R4-R7, which is what keeps the R7 index valid for 0xB2AE on the first reader path DISAGREEMENT: lightbar-bat-flow.md reads this as a 3-byte load into R0:R1:R2, pd-0x38-consumers.md reads it as four MOVX reads into R0-R3. Both are recorded; the decompile settles it. (cited from 2 files)

name: unresolved_0xB1F2
comment: Unresolved: lcalls the 3-byte loader 0x10C8 with the DPTR it was given, sets A=1 and jumps to 0x0C46. The file says the remaining control flow was not traced and deliberately did not follow the second level, so this name records a handoff and nothing more

name: unresolved_0x383A
comment: Unresolved: lcalls 0x0FCB with the DPTR it was given, clears carry and jumps to 0x0F0E. Remaining control flow not traced, for the same reason as 0xB1F2

name: write4_inline_args
comment: Described here only as one of the lcall 0x104D inline-argument routines that issue #36 owns, a framing this file takes no position on; 0x1041 immediately before it is stated to be a separate routine. No role is claimed for it | Saves the destination halves, pops its caller's return address into DPTR, calls 0x1064 four times and finishes with CLR A; JMP @A+DPTR. A linear decode through the inline constants mistakes the argument bytes for instructions (cited from 2 files)

name: switch_case_dispatch
comment: The only subroutine in the main EC image opening d0 83 d0 82 f8: it pops the return address the preceding lcall pushed into DPTR to get the inline table's address and takes the selector in A; 15 lcall sites name it and it dispatches through jmp @a+dptr at 0x716B. Keil C51's own name for the idiom is ?C?CCASE but the file says that is a name for the shape and not a symbol read out of this image

name: index_table_default
comment: Default arm of the bank0 0x8038 index dispatch: it decrements XDATA 0x08E1 and returns while that stays non-zero and when it is zero runs the longer body 0x827E-0x8293 which touches 0x1904 and 0x190C and calls 0xBCB1 before returning. The file says this is what the bytes decode to and not a claim that any of it executes

name: index_case_epilogue
comment: Shared epilogue that cases 0x00 through 0x06 of the bank0 0x8038 table jump to: it calls 0xBB08 then writes 0x06 to XDATA 0x08E1 and post-increments the selector at 0x08E0 with 0x0822C-0x0822D before an ljmp to the default 0x8274. Only the listed bytes were read and the file claims no execution order

name: index_case_00
comment: Case 0x00 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1904 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08D0 and shuffles the byte pair 0x0600/0x0601 through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x01 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: index_case_01
comment: Case 0x01 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1906 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08D2 and shuffles the byte pair 0x0602/0x0603 through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x02 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: index_case_02
comment: Case 0x02 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1909 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08D4 and shuffles the byte pair 0x0604/0x0605 through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x04 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: index_case_03
comment: Case 0x03 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table: it reads gate 0x190C and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08D6 and shuffles the byte pair 0x0606/0x0607 through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x08 of flag byte 0x0610. The per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace; §6 separately records that this address also decodes as plausible code in bank1 so bank0 is the table's bank and not a claim about which bank runs

name: index_case_04
comment: Case 0x04 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1904 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08D8 and shuffles the byte pair 0x0608/0x0609 through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x10 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: index_case_05
comment: Case 0x05 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1906 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08DA and shuffles the byte pair 0x060A/0x060B through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x20 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: index_case_06
comment: Case 0x06 handler of the bank0 0x8038 index table reached by the computed dispatch at 0x716B: it reads gate 0x1909 and ljmps to the shared default 0x8274 when bit 7 is clear; otherwise it stores an r6/r7 word into slot 0x08DC and shuffles the byte pair 0x060C/0x060D through scratch byte 0x0A59 across a call to 0xB965 and sets bit 0x40 of flag byte 0x0610. The file's per-case column is a linear decode of the window up to the next target and not a control-flow trace of the handler

name: bl51_bank_select_0
comment: Keil BL51 cross-bank switch stub that selects bank 0 in the common area: 350 of the 403 trampolines in 0x1150-0x1ABC route through it by loading DPTR with the target and jumping here. It carries the C0 08 74 prologue that occurs 4 times in the main EC image and 0 times in the PD image; nothing here is a claim about any register's behaviour

name: bl51_bank_select_1
comment: Keil BL51 cross-bank switch stub that selects bank 1 in the common area: 53 of the 403 trampolines in 0x1150-0x1ABC route through it. The audit counts bank0 calling 61 bank-1 trampolines and bank1 calling 229 bank-0 ones but does not say how these 53 split between those callers so no caller is attributed to this stub

name: bl51_bank_select_2
comment: Keil BL51 cross-bank switch stub that selects bank 2 in the common area; no trampoline in this image routes through it. The file records find_banks.py finding no trampoline callers for banks 2 and 3 which is a statement about this dump and not proof that no such caller exists

name: bl51_bank_select_3
comment: Keil BL51 cross-bank switch stub that selects bank 3 in the common area; no trampoline in this image routes through it. The file records find_banks.py finding no trampoline callers for banks 2 and 3 which is a statement about this dump and not proof that no such caller exists

name: trampoline_bank0_c881
comment: One of the 403 BL51 trampolines in the common-area block 0x1150-0x1ABC: it loads DPTR with 0xC881 and ljmps to the bank-0 select stub at 0x1100. The audit's ajmp site at 0x15BA is the 0x81 low byte of that mov dptr immediate and is a scan phantom rather than a paged branch

name: mul38_ptr_0946
comment: Construction entry for the 0x38 multiply at 0xB2B1: returns P = 0x0946 + low8(A_entry x 0x38) in DPTR, discarding the product's high byte B but keeping the base carry in DPH, and writing no R0-R7 register

name: mul38_ptr_0976
comment: Same shape as 0xB2AE with base 0x0976: returns P = 0x0976 + low8(A_entry x 0x38) in DPTR. At index 5 it discards B=01 and does not produce the full-product address 0x0A8E

name: add_a_ptr_0946
comment: Independently entered add-only suffix of the 0x38 construction: returns P = 0x0946 + A_entry and executes no MUL. Counting it as running the multiply at 0xB2B1 would erase this separate entry that the census deliberately preserves

name: mul38_of_xdata_0832
comment: Loads XDATA[0x0832], multiplies by 0x38 and returns A = low8(product) with the high product in B, leaving DPTR at 0x0832; the file states it is not itself a pointer construction. Its index load is a fresh read, not a reuse of an earlier one

name: read4xdata_to_r4_r7
comment: Four-byte XDATA reader relative to the entry pointer P: reads P..P+3 into R4..R7 with three INC DPTR and returns DPTR=P+3. It overwrites R4-R7 but not R3, and the later uses of the loaded values were not followed to any record meaning

name: add_ab_then_r7_page
comment: Calls 0x10BC to add A x B to DPTR, loads R7 into A and falls into the 0xB267 page add; it writes no R7, which is what lets the index loaded at 0x4D8D survive to 0xB2AE

name: sub_or_cmp_r0_r7
comment: Subtract/OR comparison across R0-R3 and R4-R7 that changes A/B/flags and returns ordinarily; it is the routine branched on after CLR C at 0x4DA1. What it compares, and what the loaded values mean, is not identified here

name: load_r3_r0_jmp_0f0e
comment: Loads R3..R0 from A, clears carry and tail-jumps to 0x0F0E with no intervening RET. Its R3 clobber does not invalidate the writer's source because 0x4DD6 loads R3 again

name: dispatch_code_table
comment: Complete dispatcher 0x119C..0x11C1: it consumes the return address as a CODE-table pointer, nonzero target pairs have a third selector byte and a matched selector leaves A=0 before 0x11AC, and a zero target pair selects the following default target. This framing rests on decoded dispatcher semantics plus table contents, not a raw target match

name: movc_byte_to_xdata
comment: Each invocation reads one CODE byte using MOVC, advances that pointer, swaps to the data destination for a MOVX store and increment, swaps back and returns; four calls account for exactly four inline argument bytes, not four executed caller instructions

name: dispatch_entry
comment: Prologue 0x4C27..0x4C37 immediately after RET at 0x4C26; its MOV A,R5 at 0x4C34 supplies the selector to LCALL 0x119C at 0x4C35. The framing is conditional on entry to 0x4C27: reset-to-0x4C27 reachability, all upstream callers, and occurrence of any selector are not established

name: dispatch_case_06
comment: Case 06 of the 0x119C CODE-table dispatcher (file 0x24C4A holds 4d6f06), separate from case 09 and not a successive execution region. It tests the bytes at 0x0834/0x0835 against #01, LCALLs 0xF75C and branches to 0x4DEE when the result is zero; 0x4D89 is the fallthrough of that last branch, not a separate entry

name: dispatch_case_09
comment: Case 09 of the 0x119C CODE-table dispatcher (file 0x24C4D holds 4e8409), with no sequential fallthrough into it from 0x4E7C..0x4E83. It stores A=0 to XDATA[0x083A] at entry and the gate at 0x4E8F tests that same R7-source byte against 2; j<2 on the 0x4E96 arm is a local path condition, not a global index bound
